newsitem.title: UK: Memory loss good warning of Alzheimer's - study.
newsitem.headline: Memory loss good warning of Alzheimer's - study.

text.p: Watching out for severe memory loss in elderly people is the best way to tell if they are at risk of Alzheimer's disease, U.S. researchers reported on Friday.
Of all the requirements for someone to be diagnosed with dementia, memory loss provides the most direct clue, neurologist James Bowen and colleagues at the University of Washington in Seattle said.
"Patients with severe isolated memory loss have an increased risk of developing dementia and should be closely followed up," they wrote in a report in the Lancet medical journal.
Up to a third of the elderly have some kind of dementia, Alzheimer's being the most common type. Dementia is defined as memory loss combined with some other cognitive problem such as bad judgement.

Bowen's group studied the cases of more than 800 people with mental complaints. They picked 21 patients with severe isolated memory loss and 198 who did not have memory loss but had another problem such as impaired judgement or abstract thinking.
They screened out people whose memory loss was obviously due to causes such as strokes or alcoholism.
Both groups were watched for between one and eight years. Nearly half -- 48 percent -- of the group with memory loss developed dementia while only 18 percent of the group without memory loss did.
